status: Frozen at K0 (2026-09-24), before any Rust code exists. Amendments require a dated entry in `amendments` written before Rust timings are inspected.

host.notes: 18 GB is below the ~16.5 GB kev-4b fp32 torch footprint; the 4B fp32 oracle ran a documented core subset under swap and is not benchmarked.

baseline.gdn_kernels: reference PyTorch fallbacks (causal_conv1d and flash-linear-attention not installed); upstream's own environment ships the same fallbacks on macOS CPU

workload.description: Five 3-option choice questions on a 296-token state; the shape behind upstream's M5 README table.
workload.protocol: new_state = probs_and_prefix (full pass, prefix kept); repeated_state = probs_with_prefix (branches only). Median of 20 iterations after 3 warmup, wall clock with device sync.

upstream_published_context.note: Context only, never a target: a different machine. Rust timings on this host are compared against this host's Python medians.

acceptance.k2_metal: Rust MLX median <= 1.10x the Python MLX median on this host for new_state and repeated_state on bench-m5 (kev-0.8b and, where the checkpoint fits, kev-4b); p95 no more than 5% worse than the Python p95. No speedup is assumed.
acceptance.k2_cpu: Correctness-gated only: CPU parity must hold; CPU speed is recorded, not gated.
rules: Benchmarks run on an idle host; the 1-minute load average is recorded in every result.
Result files under benchmarks/results/ are immutable; a rerun gets a new run id.
Timings taken outside an acceptance run are labelled 'not acceptance'.
No comparisons against upstream's M5 numbers are claimed as acceptance evidence.
